steps.text: This payload ran as NETWORK SERVICE and looks malicious, so I'll mark it for submission. The fax service entity id is unknown, so I'll skip that and just gather host, user, process, and command artifacts.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user wardog opened an interactive, high-integrity cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a) and used it to hijack the Fax service (T1543.003, Modify Existing Service). In order: (1) at 00:45:33 sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242) set the Fax service binPath to 'powershell.exe -noexit -c write-host T1543.003 Test'; (2) at 00:45:35 sc start Fax (proc-cd222a569d) started the service, and the Service Control Manager ran the PowerShell payload (proc-7f9f3418e9) as NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE; (3) at 00:45:41 sc.exe (proc-babd722e6c) set binPath back to C:\WINDOWS\system32\fxssvc.exe. The command line matches an Atomic Red Team test, but the technique was carried out and the payload ran under a service account, so this is treated as malicious. Response: confirm the Fax service ImagePath is back to fxssvc.exe, isolate and check the host, and rotate wardog's credentials.
